body_ar:
الدعاء على الكفار من المعلوم ضرورة أن الدعاء للمسلمين أضعف الإيمان فما حكم الدعاء على الكفار كمن يقول( رب لا تذر على الأرض من الكافرين ديارا) و كما تعلمون أن نوحا لم يدع بهذا الدعاء إلا بعد مجيء الوحي (أنه لن يؤمن من قومه إلا من قد آمن) و النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أتاه الصحابي الذي هو من دوس و قال ادع على دوس قال: اللهم اهد دوسا و ائت بهم مسلمين؟

الدعاء على الكفار هو من جهادهم و قد نفذه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقد دعا على قريش أن يؤخذوا بالسنين

اللهم اجعلها عليهم سنينا كسنين يوسف
body_en:
Supplicating against the disbelievers. It is known of necessity that supplicating for the Muslims is the weakest of faith. So what is the ruling on supplicating against the disbelievers, as in the words of one who says: {My Lord, leave not upon the earth any dweller from among the disbelievers} (Sūrat Nūḥ 71:26)? And as you know, Noah did not make this supplication until after the revelation came that {none of your people will believe except those who have already believed} (Sūrat Hūd 11:36). And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, when the Companion who was from Daws came to him and said 'Supplicate against Daws', said: 'O God, guide Daws and bring them as Muslims.'

Supplicating against the disbelievers is part of fighting them, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, carried it out: he supplicated against Quraysh that they be seized with years of famine —

'O God, make them years against them like the years of Joseph.'

flags.arabic: الدعاء على الكفار هو من جهادهم … اللهم اجعلها عليهم سنينا كسنين يوسف
flags.context: the whole of the Sheikh's published answer, which ends here
options: render faithfully, mark as a truncated excerpt, and suppress or heavily caveat it
present it as the Sheikh's ruling on supplicating against non-Muslims
present it as a partial answer
flags.note: THE MOST SERIOUS DISPLAY PROBLEM IN THIS SLICE — STYLE GUIDE §9, §10 AND §12 ALL APPLY AT ONCE. The questioner sets out a genuine tension: the Qur'an records Noah supplicating for his people's destruction, but only after revelation told him none would believe; and the Prophet, asked to supplicate against the tribe of Daws, supplicated for their guidance instead. The Sheikh's published answer consists of two clauses and a quotation, affirming that supplication against disbelievers is part of fighting them and citing a case where the Prophet did it — and then the page stops, with the rest behind the .docx download. So the record publishes the hard-line half of an answer whose qualification, reconciliation of the two cases, and conclusion are all missing. Under a title reading 'Fatwas on Jihad', in English, this is a text that will be read as the Sheikh authorising supplication for the harm of non-Muslims, without the balance his own answer evidently went on to supply. It has been translated faithfully and nothing has been added or softened. Our strong recommendation is that this record is not published in any form until someone has read the .docx and can present the complete answer.

flags.arabic: من المعلوم ضرورة أن الدعاء للمسلمين أضعف الإيمان
options: It is known of necessity that supplicating for the Muslims is the weakest of faith
It is self-evident that praying for Muslims is the least one can do
mark as a possible transcription error
flags.note: The premise as printed is odd: 'the weakest of faith' (aḍʿaf al-īmān) echoes the well-known report about denouncing wrong with the heart being the weakest of faith, but applying it to supplicating FOR Muslims does not obviously fit, and the questioner may have meant something closer to 'the least that is required'. The clause has been rendered literally. This is the questioner's wording, not the Sheikh's, and he does not take it up.

flags.arabic: و قد نفذه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
flags.context: the verb governing the Prophet's action
flags.note: naffadhahu is stronger than 'did it' — it carries the sense of executing or putting into effect, which in a sentence that has just classed the act as part of fighting gives the clause a deliberate force. Since the answer is truncated immediately afterwards, the weight the Sheikh meant this verb to carry cannot be checked against his conclusion, so the rendering is flagged as provisional.

flags.arabic: اللهم اجعلها عليهم سنينا كسنين يوسف
flags.context: the report quoted, and the last line of the published page
options: quote as the Sheikh gives it, with no narrator, collection or grading
flags.note: The Sheikh gives the report with no attribution and no grading, and the page breaks off immediately after it, so it is left standing as the final word of the record. Nothing has been supplied. Note that 'years' here means years of famine, as the reference to the years of Joseph makes clear; the English keeps the Arabic's own compression rather than glossing it, since the Sheikh's own preceding clause supplies the sense.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-27 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The first line of the body is a sub-heading in the source which runs directly into the question; kept as the source has it. The title promises fatwas on jihad in the plural and only this one is present before the break.

The two Qur'anic quotations inside the question are given in the source in round brackets without references; the references have been supplied per house style and the quotations set in the curly braces of house style, since the questioner is plainly quoting scripture.
The whole of the Sheikh's answer as published is 129 characters of Arabic. Everything else on the page is the question.
